newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN STOCKS END DOWN AS ELECTRONICS PLUNGE.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN STOCKS END DOWN AS ELECTRONICS PLUNGE.

text.p: Heavy profit-taking on red-hot electronics pulled Taiwan share prices to a lower close on Monday as institutional investors transferred holdings to constructions and steels, brokers said.
Late selling sent the index down to as low as 9,863.64 points before recovering slightly to close at 9,897.27, a loss of 96.27 points or 0.96 percent.
Turnover was heavy at T$178 billion.
Electronics, which led recent gains, encountered heavy profit-taking, plunging 5.21 percent. Microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor plunged T$8 to T$151.
Computer giant Acer fell T$5 to T$91, but notebook computer maker Twinhead International was up the daily seven percent limit to T$72 on its debut listing.
"Institutional investors, especially mutual funds, have switched some holdings to public constructions-related shares from electronics," said independent analyst Michael Hung.

As the government repeatedly vowed to accelerate public construction projects, many analysts had forecast a recovery in the domestic property market and public construction-related industries such as construction, steel and cement in the second half, Hung said.
Steels rose 2.12 percent and constructions were up 1.73 percent. Paper and chemical shares were also strong.

Construction share BES Engineering was up T$1.6 to T$42. Steel giant China Steel rose 30 cents to T$31.5 despite the government was scheduled to auction 182 million state-owned shares of China Steel in afternoon.
Brokers said the index likely would fall to test support at 9,600 since electronics encountered downward corrections.
For Tuesday, a 9,800-9,950 range was seen.
